query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thermomechanical treatment—specifically, cold rolling followed by low‐temperature controlled annealing—to the uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA will induce the formation of coherent B2 precipitates and refine its grain structure, thereby increasing both its strength and ductility and making it more resistant to extreme thermal fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading (including room-temperature creep), and corrosive environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar state of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy with insufficient strength and plasticity for industrial fastener applications.
generation.intervention: Cold rolling the alloy to introduce high dislocation density followed by low-temperature controlled annealing to stimulate the nucleation and growth of coherent B2 precipitates while retaining a refined grain structure.
generation.conditions: Performance is evaluated under fastener-relevant operating conditions including extreme temperature fluctuations, sustained mechanical loading with potential for room-temperature creep, and exposure to corrosive media.
generation.structural_mediator: The development of a microstructure with refined grains and uniformly dispersed, coherent B2 precipitates along deformation features.
generation.mechanism: Cold rolling increases dislocation density which acts as nucleation sites during annealing. The low-temperature annealing promotes the precipitation of coherent B2 particles that effectively pin the dislocations and grain boundaries. This dual effect strengthens the alloy by impeding dislocation motion and refining the grain structure, thereby enhancing yield strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion performance under cyclic temperature exposures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting alloy, the treated sample should exhibit a statistically significant increase in yield and tensile strengths with maintained or improved ductility, along with improved resistance to creep and corrosion under extreme service conditions.
generation.baseline: The as-obtained uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA without any thermomechanical treatment.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold within the processing window typical for cold rolling and low-temperature annealing (temperatures low enough to avoid excessive grain growth), and under service conditions representative of fastener applications (extreme thermal cycling, continuous mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive exposures).
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of strength and ductility improvements is uncertain due to potential variations in processing parameters and microstructural evolution. In addition, the relative contribution of the B2 precipitates compared to grain refinement in enhancing performance may vary.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloys: one subjected to the proposed cold rolling followed by low-temperature annealing and a control set with no additional thermomechanical processing. Characterize both sets using TEM and XRD to confirm the presence of coherent B2 precipitates and to measure grain size distribution. Then, conduct mechanical testing (yield strength, tensile strength, ductility, and room-temperature creep tests) and corrosion tests under simulated fastener operating conditions (extreme temperature cycling and corrosive environment exposure).
measurements: Microstructural analysis via TEM and XRD (to detect coherent B2 precipitates and determine grain size)
Mechanical properties: yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, ductility measurements, and creep rate
Corrosion performance: corrosion current density and pitting potential under standardized corrosive conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermomechanically treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant (e.g., >10%) improvement in yield strength and ductility, or if the expected coherent B2 precipitates and refined grain structure are not observed compared to the control group, then the hypothesis is considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The room-temperature strength of Al0.3CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys (HEAs) is relatively low owing to its intrinsic fcc structure. In the present study, the as-cast HEAs were subjected to cold rolling and subsequent annealing treatment (800, 900, and 1000 °C) to adjust the microstructures and tensile properties. This treatment process resulted in the partial recrystallization, full recrystallization, and grain coarsening with increasing the annealing temperature. It was found that the large and spherical B2 precipitates were generated in the recrystallized grain boundaries of three annealing states, while the small and elongated B2 precipitates were aligned along the deformation twins in the non-recrystallized region of the 800 °C-annealing state. The former B2 precipitates assisted in refining the recrystallized grains to quasi ultra-fine grain and fine grain regimes (with the grain sizes of ~0.9, ~2.2, and ~7.2 μm). The tensile results indicated that the decreased annealing temperature induced the gradual strengthening of this alloy but also maintained the ductility at the high levels. reading.lever: Apply cold rolling followed by low-temperature controlled annealing to form coherent B2 precipitates and refine grains.
reading.why: This intervention, proven in related HEA systems, directly addresses low strength and plasticity while enhancing resistance under extreme service conditions.
